records.confidence_basis: Simulator behaviour was live-tested in AMS2 1.6.9.91 with automatic clutch and shifting disabled, and the real-world transmission is supported by registered sources.

records.real_world_identity_notes: McLaren Senna, built for model years 2019 and 2020, running the 4.0-litre Ricardo-built McLaren M840TR twin-turbocharged V8 through an in-house seven-speed dual-clutch transmission.

control_notes: Simulator behaviour was directly observed in a guided drive in AMS2 1.6.9.91 with automatic clutch and shifting disabled: clutch-free move-off, automatic cut on upshifts and automatic blip on downshifts, so the driver supplies none of the three.

The car upshifts by itself. This is the gearbox rather than an assist, because automatic shifting was disabled for the drive, and it is what a road-car dual clutch does in its automatic mode. The driver therefore does not request upshifts at all, which the upshift fields, describing an automatic cut, understate. The same behaviour is recorded on the 1993 Formula HiTech Gen2 cars, whose transmissions could also be switched to fully automatic.
